title: Maize Cultivation Guide, Spacing and Nutrient Schedule
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana
content: Maize (Zea mays) thrives in well-drained, sandy loam to silty loam soils with pH 6.0 to 7.5. It cannot tolerate waterlogging even for 24-48 hours. Sowing time: Kharif (June-July with onset of monsoon), Rabi (October-November in Southern and Eastern India). Spacing and plant population: For grain hybrids, maintain 60 cm row-to-row and 20 cm plant-to-plant spacing (target plant population: 83,333 plants/ha). For sweet corn: 75 cm x 20 cm. For baby corn: 45 cm x 15 cm. Seed rate: 20 kg/ha for normal hybrids; 8-10 kg/ha for sweet corn; 25 kg/ha for baby corn. Nutrient management: Recommended N:P2O5:K2O is 120-150:60:40 kg/ha. Apply full P, K, and 20% N as basal dose. Split remaining N: 40% at knee-high stage (V6-V8, 30-35 DAS) and 40% at tasseling/silking stage (50-55 DAS). Critical irrigation stages: Knee-high stage, tasseling, silking, and grain formation. Ensure ridge-and-furrow planting to drain excess monsoon water.
